for søren.explanation: "For søren" means "goodness". To react when something surprises you, say it first: "For søren, jeg har glemt min taske!" (Goodness, I forgot my bag!)

for tiden.explanation: "For tiden" means "at the moment". To say what is true in these days, use it at the start: "For tiden er der mange biler her" (These days there are many cars here). For this very second, use "lige nu" (right now): "Jeg spiser lige nu" (I am eating right now).

foran.explanation: "Foran" means "in front of". To say where you stand, put it before the place: "Jeg står foran døren" (I stand in front of the door). To say the opposite, use "bag" (behind): "Jeg står bag døren" (I stand behind the door). Do not use "før" (before) for a place, because it is only for time: "før klokken fem" (before five o'clock).

forbavset.explanation: "Forbavset" means "astonished". To say what astonished you, add "over" (at): "forbavset over resultatet" (astonished at the result).

forbi.explanation: "Forbi" means "past". When you say something has ended, it means "over": "Sommeren er forbi" (The summer is over). To invite someone to visit, use it with "kom" (come): "Kom forbi i aften!" (Drop by tonight!)

forbløffende.explanation: "Forbløffende" means "astonishing". It describes the thing, not the person: "Resultatet er forbløffende" (The result is astonishing). To describe the person, use "forbløffet" (amazed): "Jeg er forbløffet" (I am amazed).

forbløffet.explanation: "Forbløffet" means "amazed". To say what amazed you, add "over" (at): "forbløffet over resultatet" (amazed at the result). It describes how a person feels. For the thing that causes it, use "forbløffende" (astonishing): "Det er forbløffende" (It is astonishing).

forbrug.explanation: "Forbrug" means "consumption". It comes from the verb "at forbruge" (to consume). To talk about water, put "vand" (water) in front: "Vi sænker vores vandforbrug" (We are lowering our water use).

forbudt.explanation: "Forbudt" means "forbidden". It comes from the verb "at forbyde" (to forbid). To say you may not enter a place, signs say "Adgang forbudt" (No entry).

fordelagtig.explanation: "Fordelagtig" means "advantageous". It is built from "en fordel" (an advantage). To say it pays off to do something now, use the form "fordelagtigt" with "at": "Det er fordelagtigt at købe nu" (It is advantageous to buy now).

fordomsfri.explanation: "Fordomsfri" means "unbiased". It is built from "en fordom" (a prejudice) and "fri" (free).

fordomsfuld.explanation: "Fordomsfuld" means "prejudiced". It is built from "en fordom" (a prejudice) and "-fuld" (full of).

forelsket.explanation: "Forelsket" means "in love". To say someone fell in love, use "blive" (become) and "i" (in): "Jeg blev forelsket i hende" (I fell in love with her).

foreløbig.explanation: "Foreløbig" means "for now". When something is a first version that is not final, it means "preliminary": "en foreløbig plan" (a preliminary plan).

foreningsliv.explanation: "Foreningsliv" means "club and association life". It is built from "en forening" (an association) and "et liv" (a life). The part "forening" is also in "en idrætsforening" (a sports club): "Jeg er medlem af en idrætsforening" (I am a member of a sports club).

forestående.explanation: "Forestående" means "upcoming". It is built from "fore" (ahead) and "stående" (standing), so it is literally "standing ahead".

forfra.explanation: "Forfra" means "from the beginning". When you say which side something comes from, it means "from the front": "Han kom forfra" (He came from the front). The opposite is "bagfra" (from behind): "Han kom bagfra" (He came from behind).

forfærdelig.explanation: "Forfærdelig" means "terrible". It is stronger than "dårlig" (bad): "Maden er dårlig" (The food is bad) and "Maden er forfærdelig" (The food is terrible).

forgiftet.explanation: "Forgiftet" means "poisoned". It is built from "for-" and "gift" (poison). When you describe a tense atmosphere, it also means "poisoned": "en forgiftet stemning" (a poisoned atmosphere).

forgængelig.explanation: "Forgængelig" means "transient". For food that spoils, use "letfordærvelig" (perishable) instead: "Fisk er letfordærvelig" (Fish is perishable).

forgæves.explanation: "Forgæves" means "in vain". Do not mix it up with "nytteløs" (useless), which says a thing has no use: "Det er nytteløst at skændes" (It is useless to argue).

forhastet.explanation: "Forhastet" means "hasty". It comes from the verb "at haste" (to hurry). To say someone moves fast, use "hurtig" (fast) instead: "Hun er hurtig" (She is fast).

forholdsvis.explanation: "Forholdsvis" means "relatively". It is built from "et forhold" (a ratio) and the ending "-vis". To say something is warm compared with what is normal, put it before the adjective: "forholdsvis varmt" (relatively warm).

forhåbentlig.explanation: "Forhåbentlig" means "hopefully". To say what you hope will happen, use it instead of "Jeg håber, at" (I hope that): "Jeg håber, at det bliver godt vejr" (I hope the weather will be good) becomes "Forhåbentlig bliver det godt vejr" (Hopefully the weather will be good).
